findings_addressed.oracle: Both calls must return a non-empty list with at least one model whose id contains 'gemini' (independent of each other); the set of all ids returned by call 1 must equal the set returned by call 2. An implementation that returns [] deterministically would fail the len > 0 guards; one that returns a different set on each call would fail the ids1 == ids2 assertion.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/providers/google.py _fetch_and_sort_models(), change `return sorted_models` to `return []` — both len(models1) > 0 and len(models2) > 0 assertions fail immediately.

notes: Added non-empty guards before the consistency assertion and also verified that at least one Gemini model is present in each call's results. This closes the vacuous-pass window where a broken list_models() returning [] would satisfy set() == set(). The live-cloud skip guards (google_network_required, has_google_key) are preserved.
